title: Worksheet 4: Loops (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: A loop is a programming tool that repeats a set of instructions multiple times without the programmer having to write those instructions over and over again. Loops save time and make code shorter and easier to read. For example, imagine a program needs to print the word "Hello" ten times. Instead of writing the instruction to print "Hello" ten separate times, a programmer can use a loop that says "repeat this instruction 10 times." There are different kinds of loops. A "for loop" repeats an instruction a specific, known number of times, like exactly 10 times. A "while loop" repeats an instruction as long as a certain condition remains true, such as "keep asking the user for a password while the password is incorrect." Loops are one of the most useful tools in programming because so many tasks involve repeating an action.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a loop repeats a set of instructions:
questions.correct: Multiple times, without the programmer rewriting them
distractors: Only when the user clicks a button
Only if the program has no errors

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a "for loop" repeats an instruction:
questions.correct: A specific, known number of times
distractors: Forever, until the computer is turned off
As long as a condition stays true

questions.text: According to the paragraph, a "while loop" repeats an instruction:
questions.correct: As long as a certain condition remains true
distractors: Only at the start of a program
Once for every variable in the code

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what is one benefit of using loops?
questions.correct: They save time and make code shorter and easier to read
distractors: They remove the need for variables
They make a computer's processor faster
They prevent all errors in a program

questions.text: A program must keep asking for a password until the correct one is entered, and nobody knows how many tries it will take. Based on the paragraph, which loop fits?
questions.correct: A while loop, because it repeats as long as a condition stays true
distractors: A for loop, because the number of tries is known
Neither, because loops cannot handle passwords
Both work exactly the same way here
